services.title: Product Engineering (Web)
services.shortDescription: Production-grade web applications with clean architecture, multi-tenant data models, and a roadmap that avoids rewrites.
services.description: We design and ship production-grade web applications with clean architecture, multi-tenant data models, and a roadmap that avoids rewrites.
services.whoItsFor: Founders and product leaders who want a fast MVP that can safely grow to v2/v3 without burning months on re-architecture.
problemsSolved: Fragile MVPs that can't scale or pass security reviews
Lack of analytics, testing, and deployment hygiene
deliverables: Architecture: domain + bounded contexts, API contracts (OpenAPI), modular monorepo or multi-repo
Back end: NestJS/Node or FastAPI/Python, background jobs (BullMQ/Queues), caching (Redis)
Data: Postgres/Prisma with migrations, RLS/tenant isolation, pgvector where needed
Front end: Next.js/React with a typed design system, accessibility & performance budgets
Quality: testing pyramid (unit/contract/integration), feature flags (Statsig), seed data
Ops: CI/CD (GitHub Actions), IaC (Terraform), observability (OpenTelemetry + Sentry), runbooks
Analytics: event dictionary, dashboards, KPI wiring

processTimeline.blueprint: Blueprint (1 week): scope, risks, diagrams, acceptance criteria
processTimeline.design: Design & contracts (1–2 weeks): IA, flows, API + schema contracts, tokens
processTimeline.build: Build (4–8 weeks): trunk-based dev, weekly demos, review gates
processTimeline.hardening: Hardening (1–2 weeks): load & security checks, error budgets, incident playbooks
processTimeline.launch: Launch: smoke tests, canary rollout, handover docs

technicalApproach: Favor simple, typed, boring tech; reach for Kafka/streams only when the workload needs it
Multi-tenancy via tenant_id + RLS (or schema-per-tenant for strict isolation)
Contracts first; break changes via versioned endpoints
Server-side rendering for perf/SEO; edge caching for hot paths

services.title: AI & Automation
services.shortDescription: LLM-powered features and agents that actually move metrics—designed with evaluation, guardrails, and cost control.
services.description: LLM-powered features and agents that actually move metrics—designed with evaluation, guardrails, and cost control.
services.whoItsFor: Teams with specific workflows (support, ops, finance, education, healthcare) where automation or AI assistance creates measurable savings or new value.
problemsSolved: Unclear ROI and no evaluation harness
deliverables: Use-case framing: task analysis, success metrics, failure modes
System design: RAG/agents, tool use, deterministic fallbacks
Data: retrieval stores (pgvector), embeddings strategy, redaction/PII handling
Models: OpenAI/Groq integrations, optional self-hosted (Ollama)
Guardrails: content filtering, tool constraints, human-in-the-loop steps
Eval & telemetry: offline suites, golden sets, drift alerts, prompt/version registry
Ops: cost dashboards, rate-limit and retry strategy, timeouts/circuit breakers

processTimeline.problemSpec: Problem spec (3–5 days) → define tasks, KPIs, constraints
processTimeline.thinSlice: Thin slice (1–2 weeks) → build the smallest valuable agent/feature
processTimeline.evaluation: Evaluation (1 week) → golden sets, acceptance thresholds, red-team
processTimeline.rollout: Rollout (1 week) → feature flag, audit trails, cost controls
processTimeline.scale: Scale (ongoing) → dataset curation, active learning, prompt/tool iteration

technicalApproach: Prefer tools-first agents (small, deterministic tools) over free-form chat
Retrieval with pgvector on Postgres unless scale dictates a managed vector DB
Separate safety (content policy) from capability (task); log both
Automate prompt/versioning in CI; treat prompts like code
